channel.title: Paperraft
channel.description: Research in efficient inference and AI agents, ranked by independent GitHub implementations instead of citations or stars. Papers above the attention threshold are deliberately excluded.

item.title: Online Environment Repair for Coding Agents
item.description: Online environment repair replaces reward-penalty, rollout-filtering, and static pre-training verifier hardening by asynchronously patching exploited test harnesses during RL training while leaving triggering rewards unchanged. It costs an asynchronous pipeline of candidate-repair generation (execution invariants, differential fuzzing) plus three automated validation gates per repair, adding training-time infrastructure complexity rather than inference latency or memory. It can fail if validation gates pass an incomplete patch, if repair generation misses exploit classes outside its invariants and fuzzing reach, or if the reader lacks the RL training loop it presupposes, making it inapplicable to inference-only or supervised fine-tuning workflows. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: ExpGuard: Guarding Long-Horizon LLM Agents against Corrupted Experience
item.description: ExpGuard replaces ad hoc or absent vetting of retrieved agent experiences with a task-conditioned heterogeneous graph risk predictor, counterfactual-replay risk labeling, and online repair of flagged experiences before they enter the agent's context. The costs are additional graph construction and inference at retrieval time, a matched counterfactual replay pipeline requiring checkpointed task environments for training, and ongoing maintenance of the risk model. It can fail when replay environments or checkpoints are unavailable, when risk labels misclassify subtle attacks, or when the repair step degrades legitimate experience utility and hurts task completion. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: LLM Agent Authorization Across Context Compaction
item.description: The technique replaces letting the authorizer derive its policy from the compactor's model-written summary (which conflates user text with injected content) with deriving policy only from user messages authenticated on arrival and carried verbatim across the compaction boundary, while the agent still reads the summary for context. It costs engineering effort to thread authenticated user text through the agent framework and gives the attacker a denial-of-policy option: they can block policy derivation but cannot shape it, and compaction quality for the agent itself is unchanged. It can fail where the agent framework does not expose a trust boundary between user turns and summaries, where legitimate user intent spans content that arrived as tool output rather than user text, or where authorization of requests beyond the frozen/derived per-request policy is needed. 0 independent implementations, 1 star. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: When Answering Is Administering: Permission Replies That Rewrite Coding-Agent Policy
item.description: The technique replaces unchecked acceptance of permission-prompt answers and policy updates from plugins and remote services with an enforced update step that either permits only updates preserving every currently denied call, or attributes each rule to its author and lets parties remove only their own restrictions. It costs little in memory or latency but adds enforcement logic at the shared policy-update path and constrains legitimate delegation, since without authorship records no remote party can safely relax any rule. What can fail after adoption is incomplete coverage: relays that bypass the shared update step, runtimes lacking authorship records, or agents outside the thirteen audited designs may still permit deny-rule deletion, and the vendor's indistinguishable logging of remote versus operator edits limits forensic detection. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Boundary-Aware Policy Learning for Agent-Orchestrated Robot Manipulation
item.description: Boundary-Aware Policy Learning replaces ad hoc agent-to-policy invocation, in which a visuomotor policy is called from states outside its reliable start region, with explicit shaping of a 'handoff boundary' via fine-tuning on diverse-start contact segments plus retraining on curated successful rollouts. The cost is a two-stage policy training pipeline on robot demonstration data (RoboTwin 2.0, RoboDojo) and maintenance of a handoff protocol the agent must follow, plus compute for iterative self-improvement retraining. The method can fail when deployment tasks or embodiments differ from training distributions, and its gains are validated only in simulation benchmarks rather than on physical hardware. 0 independent implementations, 222 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: SkillCore: Internalizing Generalizable Skills via Scaffolding-Removed Fine-Tuning
item.description: SkillCore replaces runtime skill loading—external procedural guidance injected into agent prompts—with supervised fine-tuning on agent trajectories whose skill-loading scaffolding has been removed, so the model executes the procedures directly. The cost is building a trajectory transformation and mixing pipeline plus an SFT run (feasible for an 8B model on a 24 GB GPU with parameter-efficient methods, harder for 72B), and the quality risk of baking skills into weights that must be refreshed as procedures change. Failure modes include catastrophic forgetting of general coding ability if the scaffold-removed-to-skill-native mixture ratio is wrong, loss of task-specific skill invocation, and internalized procedures becoming stale or inapplicable on out-of-distribution tasks. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: distillation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: TimeTravelContainer: A Live Forking Sandbox for Stateful Agent Exploration
item.description: TTC replaces session checkpointing to disk and relaunch-from-scratch with rootless copy-on-write live forking of an entire container, including processes, memory, filesystem, and network. It costs little in memory because read-only pages are shared after the fork, but it introduces a custom container runtime into the agent harness, adding integration and operational complexity. It can fail with tools whose state lives outside the container (external services, licenses, GPUs, kernel resources), with workloads that write heavily after the fork and erase the CoW savings, and with correctness or isolation gaps in a young runtime that has so far been evaluated only on two EDA flows. 0 independent implementations, 2 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Norn: Context-Length-Aware Optimization of Weight and KV Cache Placement for Offloaded LLM Inference
item.description: Norn replaces static weight and KV-cache offloading schedules (as in FlexGen-style pipelined sharding) with context-length-aware execution plans that switch at precomputed points during decoding, plus operator-major chunked prefill to avoid repeated weight transfers. The cost is an offline profiling and plan-generation phase per model and hardware pair, sublayer-level scheduling complexity, and reliance on compute-transfer overlap that ties it to a specific inference-engine implementation rather than a drop-in configuration. It can fail if the workload's context lengths do not cross the precomputed switching points, if host-to-GPU bandwidth differs from the profiling assumptions, if the implementation is not publicly available or maintained, or if the reported speedups do not transfer beyond the two Qwen3 models and systems evaluated. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: test.

item.title: SPRUNN: Structural Proximity for Pruning in Deep Neural Networks
item.description: SPRUNN replaces magnitude-based or heuristic filter-importance criteria with a structural-proximity measure that compares each convolutional filter against all others to identify redundant filters, combined with fine-grained pruning of fully connected layers and a refined learning-rate schedule during retraining. It costs an offline pruning-plus-retraining pipeline: compute for filter-similarity computation, fine-tuning cycles to recover accuracy, and added complexity in maintaining a pruned variant alongside the base model; on a single GPU this is feasible but adds engineering effort. It can fail when similarity-based importance does not match true sensitivity, producing accuracy drops that retraining cannot fully recover, and when unstructured FC sparsity yields no wall-clock speedup on standard dense kernels, so realized latency gains depend on structured filter removal and hardware support. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Beyond Hard Tokens: Predictive Memory for Multimodal Protein Generation
item.description: PredMem replaces the stateless mask reset in iterative masked decoding of multimodal protein language models, carrying a probability-weighted Top-k expectation embedding of uncommitted predictions forward as a soft anchor instead of resetting unresolved sites to an identical [MASK] embedding. It costs nothing in extra denoiser forward passes or training; the only overhead is summarizing logits and an affine interpolation into masked inputs, plus new hyperparameters (k and the interpolation weight) to tune. It can fail if the stabilized early trajectories entrench poor initial beliefs, if the reader's workloads are anchored/conditional rather than open-ended co-generation where gains are claimed, or if it is applied outside the masked discrete diffusion decoding setting where the mechanism does not transfer. 0 independent implementations, 3 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Can AI Design a Better nnU-Net? A Hypothesis-Driven Architecture Discovery Loop from Failures to Design Rules
item.description: The method replaces manual nnU-Net architecture tuning and scalar-fitness neural architecture search with an LLM-driven loop that diagnoses structured failures, tests falsifiable hypotheses under a frozen pipeline, and distills validated mechanisms into executable trigger-to-action rules; the distilled result is a leaner architecture (LeanNeXt/LeanNeXt+) that reallocates computation to the mid-encoder and applies support-confined region contrast. It costs the engineering effort of running an eight-wave agent search with counterfactual controls plus 3D segmentation training runs, which on a single 24 GB GPU means significant wall-clock time, and it adds trigger-routing complexity at inference. It can fail when the reader's anatomy, modality, or dataset differs from the CT/MRI settings where the triggers were validated, when the discovered rules do not transfer outside the frozen nnU-Net pipeline assumptions, or when the single-source benchmark improvements do not replicate on the reader's data. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Factorized Context Attention: From Emulated to Native Grid Probing
item.description: Factorized Context Attention replaces grid probing's repeated per-span re-encoding with a native block-sparse attention pass that encodes the input once into a shared KV cache and reads all local and strided spans in one batched forward. It costs a custom attention implementation with masking plus a stair position schedule, rather than any training or extra parameters. It can fail where the block-sparse pattern is unsupported by the reader's inference stack, where spans straddle the trained position range despite the schedule, or where tasks need dense cross-span interactions that strided probing misses. 1 independent implementation, 7 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: See the Answer, Learn to Embed: Learning Universal Multimodal Embeddings from Hindsight
item.description: HEME replaces inference-time intermediate reasoning in multimodal embedding models with a hindsight-distilled student: a teacher trained with access to the paired candidate (via a hindsight attention mask, mismatched-candidate conditioning, and query-token alignment) is frozen and its representation and similarity distribution are distilled into a student that encodes queries and candidates independently. The cost is entirely at training time: an extra teacher model, a distillation stage, and the associated data and GPU budget, while inference cost stays at that of a standard single-pass embedder. Failure modes include residual candidate leakage or representation collapse if the teacher's safeguards underperform, and degraded generalization when the distillation data does not match the deployment domain. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: distillation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: MAGPIE: Agentic Multi-Reference Image Generation via Executable Scene Construction
item.description: MAGPIE replaces implicit compositional guidance (prompts, layouts, reference conditioning alone) in multi-reference image generation with an executable Blender scene that a coding agent builds, verifies against the instruction, and iteratively revises; the verified proxy render then guides a generator fine-tuned on MAGPIE-Instruct-3K. Costs include a Blender runtime plus a coding-agent loop adding latency and API spend per image, extra infrastructure to maintain, and generator fine-tuning on a custom 3K dataset. It can fail when the coding agent produces geometrically wrong scenes that its own checking misses, when subjects not covered by the dataset drift in appearance, and when the Blender dependency or agent-iteration latency is unacceptable in a production path. 0 independent implementations, 19 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: VISE: Verifier-Independent Skill Self-Evolution with Feedback from Tool Implementations
item.description: VISE replaces task-specific verifiers as the feedback source for refining agent skill files, instead comparing tool implementations (capabilities, inputs, usage conditions, output formats) against current SKILL.md instructions to propose targeted edits. The cost is an additional LLM-driven revision stage per skill evolution cycle, plus engineering to extract and parse tool source code and execution traces, which fits within a single-GPU or API budget. It can fail when tool source code is unavailable or undocumented, when implementation details diverge from actual runtime behavior, or when incorrect edit recommendations degrade previously working skills, since the reported gains are relative to no-verifier baselines on two specific benchmarks. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: HiCal: Offline Calibration for Hierarchical Scale Encoding in Accurate HiF4 Quantization
item.description: It replaces the fixed rounding rule and scale-extension thresholds of standard HiF4 block floating-point quantization with offline-calibrated rounding bias and empirically optimized Level-2/Level-3 thresholds, keeping the deterministic per-block encoding unchanged at inference. It costs only a one-time offline calibration on representative tensor statistics, with no added inference latency, no per-block candidate search, and no extra memory; the residual cost is implementation effort in the quantization pipeline. It can fail if the deployment target lacks HiF4 hardware or kernel support, if calibration data distributions drift from production activations, and the reported end-to-end gains (about one percentage point) may be too small to survive integration overhead. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: ModelLess: A Serverless System for Multi-Tier LLM Inference on Shared GPUs
item.description: ModelLess replaces per-product static GPU provisioning with platform-owned serverless instances that sleep with weights in host memory and free GPUs for lower-priority tiers under explicit eviction semantics. It costs a custom four-component stack (entry, dispatcher, node agent, SGLang plugin), a preemption protocol with durable re-enqueue, and host memory to hold sleeping weights, and its benefit collapses if wake takes minutes rather than seconds. It can fail through the unevaluated job tier and follow/seal path, sensitivity to idle-threshold tuning for long-tail services, and the fact that all savings figures are idealized trace-replay upper bounds rather than production measurements. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: TeamFlowRL: Online Policy Optimization of Decentralized Flow Policies for Multi-Agent Coordination
item.description: TeamFlowRL replaces Gaussian-policy online fine-tuning of offline-pretrained generative (flow) policies with team-level policy optimization over complete denoising trajectories, sidestepping intractable action likelihoods by weighting per-agent trajectory ratios with a shared team advantage. It costs a two-stage pipeline: offline multi-agent flow pretraining on demonstration trajectories followed by online RL with environment access, plus simulation infrastructure and per-agent ratio clipping machinery. It can fail where no simulator or reward signal exists, where offline datasets are unavailable, and its gains are demonstrated only in simulation benchmarks, so transfer to real systems is unvalidated. 0 independent implementations, 9 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: ICLWorld: Benchmarking In-Context Learning of Agents from Digital to Physical Worlds
item.description: ICLWorld replaces offline, text- or static-image-based, contamination-prone agent evaluations with an online benchmark of 160 tasks across 30 digital and physical environments, accessed through a unified UI harness. Adoption costs are the engineering effort to integrate the UIverse harness, API inference expense for frontier models across 630 demonstrations and three rule versions per task, and potential licensing or access constraints for the robot environments. It can fail to predict production behavior if the reader's tasks do not involve learning counter-intuitive rules from context, and results on six specific frontier models may not transfer to the models the reader actually deploys. 1 independent implementation, 138 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Bathys: Advancing Deep Search Agents
item.description: The technique replaces single-pass retrieval or shallow agentic search with a trained deep search agent that iteratively reformulates queries, gathers evidence chains, and verifies answers via an SFT, KTO, and compaction-managed RL pipeline. It costs a full post-training stack: verifiable question synthesis with indirect-reference clues, curated trajectories, online RL with context compression, and model sizes (9B–27B) that exceed a single 24 GB GPU for training and strain it even for inference without quantization. After adoption, the reported scores depend on trajectory self-verification and conditional retries, so reproduction without that evaluation protocol, or with weaker base models and less curated data, is likely to underperform the claimed numbers. 1 independent implementation, 126 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Economic World Model
item.description: The framework replaces purely hand-specified structural economic models and direct LLM policy decisions with a hybrid pipeline: household policies learned from microdata, a calibrated structural transition model from macro data, and a simulator an LLM agent queries before acting. It costs a full modelling and calibration effort over proprietary micro and macro datasets, plus an evaluation stack for distributions, forecasts, and counterfactuals; the LLM planning gain is small, simulation-bound, and validated only against a benchmark life-cycle model's short-run transmission. It can fail through distribution shift between training data and deployment conditions, misspecified structural transitions that invalidate counterfactuals, and simulated-GDP gains that do not transfer to real economic outcomes. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: ReQOR: Operator-Discrepancy Subspace Repair for Quantization-Conditioned Backdoors in Large Language Models
item.description: Replaces security-guided quantization configuration selection and iterative gradient-based backdoor mitigation with a training-free repair: it measures per-module operator discrepancies between full-precision and quantized versions on identical states from the quantized trajectory, extracts dominant discrepancy directions on benign calibration data, and restores full-precision computation along those directions via a closed-form factorized residual adapter. Costs are a calibration pass over benign data plus, for full-span repair, extra memory to store the adapters; the low-rank variant reduces this overhead but may repair less completely. It can fail when the backdoor's discrepancy energy lies outside the identified dominant subspace, when calibration data do not activate the relevant directions, or against attacks whose mechanism does not manifest as local same-state operator discrepancies. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Measuring Layer-wise Intrinsic Dimensionality of FFNs in LLMs via PCA
item.description: Replaces the uniform FFN intermediate width convention (and uniform-width pruning) with per-layer widths allocated by PCA-measured intrinsic dimensionality, trained via knowledge distillation under a matched parameter budget. Costs a PCA calibration pass over a corpus, a distillation training run, and added architecture heterogeneity that complicates kernel and serving assumptions. Can fail when the teacher has low dimensionality dispersion (gains shrink to ~0.5 points), when the post-training distribution shifts activations away from the calibration profile, or when irregular per-layer widths negate inference efficiency on standard hardware. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: What Does a Skill Vocabulary Cost? A Closed-Loop Decomposition over Demonstrated Motions
item.description: MPQ replaces the jointly learned latent codebook inside a skill policy with an external library of demonstrated motion prototypes, snapping each predicted action chunk to its nearest library element and correcting it toward the prediction within a bound, with no trained parameters. It costs a nearest-neighbor lookup and stored demonstration library at execution time, adds no training overhead, and the paper reports no measurable closed-loop performance loss across six architectures including a 7B VLA model. It can fail to transfer if the library does not cover the deployment distribution, and its offline reconstruction metrics are shown to misjudge library size, design, and cross-benchmark transfer, so validation must be closed-loop. 1 independent implementation, 222 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: MXFP4 for LLM Inference: Complementary Post-Training Quantization Techniques and Their Interactions
item.description: The method replaces BF16 or generic one-size-fits-all 4-bit post-training quantization with format-dependent recipes combining microscaling formats (MXFP4, MXFP6, NVFP4), Hadamard rotation, error-correcting PTQ, and the calibration-free Midmax scale selection for power-of-two block scales. Costs are added PTQ pipeline complexity, per-format tuning effort, and modest activation memory overhead if MXFP6 activations are used to recover accuracy; Midmax itself adds no calibration cost. Failure modes include applying MXFP4-tuned techniques (rotation, error-correcting PTQ) to NVFP4 where they yield little benefit, relying on per-tensor macroscales that the paper shows do not help MXFP4, and residual clipping error from E8M0 block scales on outlier-heavy models. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Scalable Placement for Disaggregated LLM Serving on Heterogeneous Edge Fleets
item.description: Spade replaces genetic-search or exhaustive placement planning for disaggregated prefill/decode LLM serving with a dominance-pruned combinatorial search combining water-filling layer partitioning and a bounded multidimensional knapsack under a congestion-aware objective. The cost is implementing a custom planner: the device model, dominance-pruning logic, and knapsack solver must be integrated into the serving stack and re-run when fleet composition or demand shifts. It can fail when real workloads deviate from the synthetic bursty-demand model used for evaluation, when the fleet is too small or homogeneous for disaggregation to pay off, or when the objective's congestion proxy misestimates actual queueing latency. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Reading Decisions Before Spans: Efficient Generative Verification
item.description: Prefill1 replaces full generative verification output (quote-and-classify error lists) with prefilled fixed syntax tokens plus a single generated branch token, stopping decoding at the empty-list versus first-error decision point. It requires a frozen 2B verifier with a rigid structured output schema and known fixed token prefix, adding prompt-construction logic but no training; quality is near-identical (F1 83.43 vs 83.41) yet the paper reports small decision changes, and 6.74-26.73% savings under compiled execution rather than the headline 84.84%. It fails when downstream consumers need error localization or quoted spans, when the output schema or instruction changes (invalidating the prefilled prefix), or when the early branch decision diverges from what full decoding would have produced. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: test.

item.title: ShellBench: What Matters More for AI Agents, Models, or Harness for Everyday Tasks
item.description: ShellBench replaces ad hoc agent configuration selection with a standardized benchmark of 100 realistic day-to-day tasks graded for correctness and safety across 12 models, 5 harnesses, and 3 reasoning levels. Adopting its guidance costs little directly, but acting on it requires running one's own representative tasks through candidate model-harness pairs, since benchmark tasks may not match the reader's distribution. Its findings can fail to transfer because only 20% of tasks are public, results cover 2026-era proprietary models, and harness differences were small only within the five harnesses tested. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: SpecEngineeringBench: Evaluating Coding Agents as Autonomous Specification Engineers
item.description: It replaces ad hoc evaluation of coding agents on cued test-generation tasks (issue descriptions, designated test entry points) with an uncued benchmark of 100 instances across 78 Python repositories measuring defect discovery and fault localization. Cost is limited to agent API calls and harness setup for test execution, coverage, and localization scoring, with no training or cluster requirement. It can fail as a selection signal if teams read pass rate or coverage as evidence of defect-finding ability, since the paper shows these metrics decouple and function-level localization remains near 51%. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: AVQ-Attention-2: Adaptive Vector-Quantized Attention with Exact Local Blocks and Linear-Cost Training
item.description: It replaces exact quadratic attention in pretrained transformers with an approximate layer that clusters keys, attends to exact local blocks plus per-cluster key means, and can be dropped in without fine-tuning. Costs include O(NM) compute in both training and inference, the added complexity of codebook maintenance and cluster-assignment logic, and a custom kernel implementation outside the standard FlashAttention stack. Failure modes include quality degradation on workloads where attention mass does not concentrate in few clusters, approximation error accumulating across layers, and integration risk if no maintained implementation exists for the reader's inference framework. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: attention and kernels. Recommendation: test.

item.title: LEGOSpec: A Composable and Efficient Framework for Speculative Draft Design and Training
item.description: LEGOSpec replaces monolithic speculative-draft recipes (EAGLE-style fixed designs trained under mismatched conditions) with a composable Context/Backbone/Proposal/Objective framework, and its DFlux configuration replaces the strongest existing baseline draft. The cost is a draft-training pipeline (supervision data from the target model, plus training compute that the framework makes up to 79% more efficient), additional inference memory for the draft, and integration complexity in the serving stack; adoption via the draft adds negligible per-token latency only when acceptance is high. It can fail when the workload shifts (backbone choice is context- and memory-dependent, so a draft tuned for short contexts underperforms on long ones), when the target model differs from the Qwen/Gemma families evaluated, or when proposal latency outweighs acceptance gains at small batch sizes. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Leto: Utility-Centric Agent Memory
item.description: Leto replaces fidelity-based agent memory (store faithful summaries, retrieve by similarity) with utility-centric memory: index conversation sources, replay anticipated context per request, and refine selection using response outcomes. It costs an indexing and replay pipeline plus an outcome-feedback utility loop, adding system complexity and per-request retrieval overhead, though it can reduce served context tokens relative to raw-history retrieval. It can fail when future requests diverge from what the replay anticipates, when the outcome signal is noisy or unavailable, or on workloads without recurring user context where simpler retrieval suffices. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Train What You Run: Probabilistic Convolutions for Learning Token Compaction in State Space Models
item.description: ProbConv replaces heuristic or post-hoc token pruning in Mamba-style state space backbones by computing the exact expected convolution under independent keep probabilities, making token keep decisions differentiable during training. The cost is a modified training procedure with a custom operator and the need to retrain the target backbone rather than applying the method to a frozen or API-served model; inference itself uses the standard compacted block with binary decisions. It can fail when the reader cannot retrain the model, when backbones lack local convolutions (standard transformers are out of scope), or when compaction is light, since the reported advantage concentrates under strong token removal. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Can LLM Judges Catch Unsafe Clinical Actions? A Fault-Injection Study
item.description: The technique replaces trusting an agent's self-reported success or answer-only LLM grading with trajectory-level LLM judging augmented by a rule-based checker grounded in the actual environment state (here, EHR responses). The cost is additional inference per evaluated trajectory, engineering of domain-specific rules, and the need to expose full tool outputs to the judge; including the agent's reasoning adds tokens without improving detection and degrades detection of misreported values by 0.18. It can fail on errors that leave the final answer unchanged, on incorrectly reported clinical values (the hardest category, missed even with reasoning traces), and on domain-model judges that miss dangerous cases such as medication overdoses, so judges alone cannot be the safety boundary. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Can a Frontier LLM Repair a Quantized Network by Tool-Free Weight-Space Programming?
item.description: Replaces data-driven PTQ rounding optimizers (e.g., AdaRound) and the calibration data they require with a single frontier-LLM API call that reasons over text-serialized weights to balance rounding errors per kernel. Costs API tokens proportional to parameter count, depends on a frontier proprietary model, requires prompt engineering per protocol, and yields accuracy 2.8 points below AdaRound while still losing 3.5 points to the float baseline. Fails when given only the float network (LLMs revert to plain RTN), does not scale beyond tiny networks because weights must fit in context, and offers no guarantee of generalization to production-scale architectures. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Latent Merger: Latent-Space Composition of Hypernetwork-Generated LoRAs
item.description: Latent-space LoRA merging replaces storing one LoRA adapter per document by composing the hypernetwork's intermediate latents and decoding them into a single fixed-rank adapter. It costs a dependency on an existing hypernetwork pipeline (Doc-to-LoRA or SHINE) and its frozen generation head, adding no serving-time memory beyond one adapter but requiring the hypernetwork infrastructure to be trained and maintained. It can fail because the approach depends on the specific spectral structure of hypernetwork-generated LoRAs, so gains may not transfer to directly fine-tuned adapters, and the abstract reports only qualitative improvements without quantified retention of per-document knowledge. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Shifter Quantization: Compact Representations for Native Integer Computation
item.description: Shifter Quantization replaces standard groupwise weight quantization by reconstructing native-width integer operands via shared appended and shifted bits, enabling standard INT MMA to span the full dot product, with an SHI variant using INT4 kernels. It requires adopting a new weight format and its associated custom kernels rather than using off-the-shelf llama.cpp or vLLM quantization paths. Adoption can fail if the released kernels lack support for the reader's models, GPU architecture, or serving framework, or if the reported throughput gains do not reproduce on different hardware and workloads. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: AIChipBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Automated AI Accelerator Design
item.description: AIChipBench replaces ad hoc or output-only evaluation of LLM coding agents for hardware design with an executable integer reference that exposes stored-state mismatches at every decoding step, plus held-out grading on new token sequences, resets, memory stalls, and synthesis. It costs the effort of building step-level reference state and substantially expanded final test suites rather than relying on public output tests, and it does not itself provide an adoptable tool or model. The demonstrated failure mode is directly relevant to agent evaluation generally: designs pass output tests while corrupting internal state, with 45 of 69 accepted designs failing under regrading, so any agentic workflow the reader adopts should use state-level or intermediate feedback and final tests well beyond development cases. 1 independent implementation, 128 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Delegent: A Multi-Agent Harness That Reduces Cost without Sacrificing Performance
item.description: Replaces the practice of the frontier model re-reading its full context and executing every subtask itself, by keeping the frontier model in charge while delegating focused subtasks (code investigation, test execution, corpus search) to a locally hosted SLM, without training a router or cascade. Costs include running an SLM (a 27B FP8 model, or a 2B model that fits on a laptop) alongside the frontier API, plus the engineering complexity of a multi-agent harness built on Claude Code. The savings depend on workload legwork, so tasks dominated by hard reasoning see little benefit, and a weak SLM without the constraining instruction can lose tasks or return errors the frontier model must absorb. 0 independent implementations, 2 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Draft Calibration for Speculative Decoding: Accelerating LLM Serving by Matching Draft and Target Distributions
item.description: Draft calibration replaces the raw, typically underconfident draft-model distribution used in speculative decoding with a post-hoc calibrated version (standard temperature scaling or token-wise calibration) that better matches the target distribution and raises token acceptance. It costs essentially nothing in memory or latency, adding only a temperature-fitting step over calibration data and negligible per-token computation, with no quality loss since target verification remains unchanged. It can fail if the draft-target pair is already well calibrated, if the fitted temperature does not transfer across tasks or sampling conditions, or if the serving stack does not use speculative decoding at all, in which case the technique has nothing to improve. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: The Growth Path Is the Missing Half of Neural Networks
item.description: It replaces post-hoc pruning or separate architecture search with an always-on second pathway: a conserved per-layer nutrient budget redistributed by usage makes units divide or die during ordinary gradient training, with a single number setting network size. The cost is additional per-step allocation computation, implementation complexity inside the training loop, and behavioral dependence on the optimizer, with reported gains under Adam but much weaker or null results under plain SGD. It can fail by trading compute against rarely used content at deployment, by only tying equal-size baselines on one continual-learning stream, and by not transferring beyond the small MLP regime in which it was demonstrated. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: MotionServe: Efficient Multi-Robot Serving by Exploiting Robot Execution Slack
item.description: MotionServe replaces per-robot dedicated GPUs or naive shared-GPU dispatch of VLA policies with LoRA-shared backbones plus coordinated observation triggering (MotionExec) and slack-aware batch scheduling (SlackBatch). It costs the engineering complexity of a custom scheduler tied to action-chunk semantics and requires LoRA-compatible policies sharing a frozen backbone, which constrains model and adaptation choices. It can fail when GPU-work estimates are inaccurate or motion-structure triggers misfire, since exhausted execution slack produces robot stalls and early observation can cause disruptive replanning that lowers task success; results are validated only in simulation on two VLA models. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: PCC: Pivotal Channel Compensation for Layer Pruning of Large Language Models
item.description: PCC replaces costlier post-pruning compensation (such as fine-tuning-based recovery) with small learnable linear transformations applied to a few pivotal channels at the pruning interface after removing whole transformer layers. It costs a small number of extra parameters and a modest training pass for the compensation matrices, and it presupposes that layer pruning is already being used. It can fail if the pivotal-channel concentration assumption does not hold for the target model, if the pruned model's degradation exceeds what channel-level linear compensation can recover, or if the compression target does not actually require layer pruning rather than quantization or KV-cache reduction. 1 independent implementation, 130 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: PackLoop: Row-Packed Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Language Models under Concurrency
item.description: PackLoop replaces wavefront-style pipelined self-speculative scheduling for looped language models with row-packed scheduling, in which speculative positions are accumulated and advanced together within a single KV-cache row read, plus an EOQ-based admission rule that decides accumulation length. It costs a new scheduling engine calibrated once per deployment, continued dependence on a self-speculative proposer (context-copy proposals), and FP32 execution to guarantee token-for-token exactness with autoregressive decoding, all tied to the Ouro family of looped models. It can fail if the reader's models are standard transformers rather than looped models, if GPU or engine details invalidate the calibrated cost model, or if exactness is relaxed, in which case output divergence under sampling and early exit is no longer guaranteed. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: EdgeALM: An Efficient and Unified Edge Accelerator for Large Audio Language Models via Full-Stack Hardware-Software Co-Design and Agent-Driven Recursive Optimization
item.description: EdgeALM replaces GPU-based ALM inference with a custom FPGA accelerator combining AWQ-style quantization, modality-conditioned vocabulary pruning, a Conv-Matmul disaggregated architecture, and an extra-coarse-grained ISA, all tuned by agent-driven recursive optimization. It costs the purchase and bring-up of an Alveo U50-class FPGA plus reliance on a bespoke compiler/toolchain and an agent-driven tuning loop, and requires accepting quantization and vocabulary pruning of the target model. It can fail if the compression flow degrades accuracy on the reader's specific audio models, if the custom software stack proves fragile or unmaintained, or if model updates outpace the hardware-specific optimization loop. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Low-Rank Tensor Representations for Efficient Multimarginal Optimal Transport
item.description: LRMOT replaces full high-dimensional transport-plan tensors in multimarginal optimal transport with plans constrained to bounded multilinear rank, using low-rank tensor representations to avoid exponential memory growth in the number of marginals. The cost is a rank hyperparameter that must be chosen per problem, plus approximation error relative to the exact MOT solution that is bounded theoretically but workload-dependent in practice. It can fail when the true optimal coupling has high multilinear rank, in which case the low-rank restriction materially degrades solution quality, and it offers no benefit if the application does not involve multimarginal transport. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Toward a Scalable and Adaptive Evaluation Measure for Time Series Anomaly Detection
item.description: FastVUS replaces the standard VUS implementation (and the threshold-dependent Precision/Recall or threshold-independent AUC metrics VUS itself supersedes) with an exact reformulation using parallel buffer computation, buffer pruning, a single reduced matrix multiplication for the confusion matrix, one-pass buffer evaluation, and a global mask over non-anomalous regions; AutoVUS additionally replaces fixed buffer lengths with per-detection adaptive selection against a random baseline. The cost is negligible for constrained infrastructure: it is a CPU evaluation library with an optional GPU path that fits trivially in 24 GB, plus implementation complexity in adapting existing pipelines to the new API and validating the GPU variant's small approximation error. Failure modes include mis-ranking detectors if AutoVUS's random-baseline buffer selection behaves unexpectedly on datasets with unusual anomaly-length distributions, silent divergence of the approximate GPU path beyond its tested error bound, and wasted effort if the reader's production systems do not perform time series anomaly detection at all. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Time Series Foundation Models on the Edge
item.description: Replaces full recomputation or linearly growing KV caches at each forecast refresh with a persistent fixed-size recurrent state for causal time series foundation models, verified equivalent to full recomputation. Costs are limited to implementing state persistence per architecture and accepting that only recurrent models (TiRex-2 among the nine tested) fully satisfy accuracy, latency, and memory requirements; attention-based models still grow linearly. Can fail because most models lose accuracy beyond their trained context length, so long histories may not improve forecasts and accuracy retention must be validated on the target data before deployment. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: ANOR: Scaling Sparse Attention with a GPU-PNM Computing Hierarchy
item.description: ANOR replaces PNM-centric sparse-attention execution, in which the near-memory device computes most of the attention and becomes the bottleneck, with a GPU-centric tiering scheme: the GPU serves attention from a cache of recently selected KV entries, the CXL-PNM device handles only cache misses, and a bounded update policy plus an Early Streaming Buffer limit link traffic and redundant DRAM reads. Its costs are the need for CXL-PNM hardware, added system complexity across two compute tiers, GPU memory reserved for the KV selection cache, and an adaptive cache-factor mechanism that trades hit ratio against batch size under varying load. It can fail if the workload lacks the selection locality the GPU cache depends on, if miss rates exceed what the low-bandwidth PNM tier can absorb, or if CXL link saturation negates the decoupling of cache updates from decode execution. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: CGSpec: Consistency-Guided Speculative Decoding with Overlap-Aware Verification Scheduling for Edge-Cloud Inference
item.description: CGSpec replaces standard collaborative speculative decoding with static speculative budgets and naive shared-verifier scheduling by adding divergence-guided adaptive budgets, nomination-and-competition tree construction, and overlap-aware request scheduling. It costs additional verifier-side bookkeeping, client return-time estimation, and coordination logic between edge drafters and the cloud verifier. It can fail when divergence estimates misjudge draft-target agreement, when network heterogeneity invalidates return-time predictions, or in single-client deployments where the scheduling gains do not materialize. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: When an AI agent makes a mistake in a database, what decides the damage?
item.description: The study replaces intuition about guard layers and model choice with a scripted mistake library (22 canonical errors) and engine-native recovery drills across 12 engines and permission/recovery arms, showing damage is governed mainly by engine permissions and undo capability rather than the model. It costs nothing to adopt as knowledge, but operationalizing it means enforcing least-privilege credentials, tested backups, and engine-specific recovery procedures rather than relying on a guard layer whose benefit was not consistently supported. Its conclusions can fail to transfer because the post-hoc analyses (S1-S13) are exploratory and uncorrected, the preregistered outcome and original-row loss disagree about the guard layer on four engines, and one hypothesis was uninformative because agents never found the credential. 0 independent implementations, 2 stars. Research area: failure recovery. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Revisiting LLMs as Context Engineers
item.description: Automated LLM-as-context-engineer (LCE) methods replace manual prompt and instruction engineering by having the LLM distill generalizable instructions or experiences from offline trial trajectories. Their cost is additional offline generation over trials plus longer engineered contexts at inference, adding latency and token spend. The paper shows these methods fail when failure modes in reasoning trajectories are diverse (gains correlate negatively with failure-mode diversity, r=-0.5), do not reliably beat chain-of-thought, and do not consistently improve with more parameters or iterations, so adopting them in production is not supported by this evidence. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: sudo L7: Can Coding Agents Act Like Staff Engineers?
item.description: sudo L7 replaces ad hoc or test-pass-only evaluation of coding agents with 60 staff-engineer-authored tasks graded against 1,287 hidden atomic rubric criteria spanning eight behavioral dimensions, including truthful reporting and risk flagging. Adopting it costs nothing in infrastructure since results are on a public leaderboard, but replicating the grading methodology internally requires an agentic grader that reads transcripts, runs code, and treats test output as evidence, which adds evaluation pipeline complexity. It can fail as a selection tool because tasks are built around prior frontier-model failures in mostly private codebases, so scores may not transfer to the reader's domain, and model grader agreement with humans is only 85-86%, leaving roughly one in seven criterion verdicts unreliable. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: DelayOPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation from a Synchronous Teacher for Real-time Asynchronous Policies
item.description: DelayOPSD replaces naive asynchronous execution of flow-based VLA policies (or training on expert demonstrations alone) by distilling a synchronous teacher, derived from the same policy with current observations, into a delayed student on the student's own rollouts, matching the teacher throughout the denoising process. It costs an additional rollout-generation and fine-tuning phase with a teacher forward pass per delayed step, but adds no modules or latency at deployment. It can fail if on-policy rollouts are expensive or unsafe to collect, if the teacher's own synchronous behavior is already weak, or if the delay regime in production exceeds the delay trained for. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: distillation. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Learning What to Change: State-Verified Reinforcement Learning for Educational Agents
item.description: State-Verified Reinforcement Learning replaces text-level LLM judges and isolated tool-call checks as the reward source for agent training, instead supervising GRPO with deterministic verification of workspace state transitions, workflow ordering, and side effects, gated by hard zero reward on critical violations. It costs an isolated sandbox per episode that snapshots state around every tool call, a deterministic verifier, 1,000 verifiable training instances, an evidence-grounded judge for saved artifacts, and full online RL training of a 27B model, all of which exceed constrained single-GPU infrastructure. After adoption it can fail when the verifier's notion of a critical violation is incomplete or mis-specified, since reward hacking shifts to whatever state properties the verifier does not audit, and gains may not transfer beyond the 11 educational categories and 16 native tools used for training. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Quantizing Diffusion LLMs under Parallel Decoding: Commitment Risk and the Parallelism Tax
item.description: DECAL replaces standard layer-wise W4A4 post-training calibration (performed under fixed-step samplers) with commitment-risk-reweighted calibration measured on the deployed cached parallel decoder, plus an argmax-preserving commit temperature that recovers the extra forward passes quantization causes. It costs an offline commitment-risk measurement on the deployed decoder and a small change to the commit rule; memory footprint stays at W4A4 and no retraining is required. It can fail if the production decoder configuration drifts from the one used for calibration, if the model is not a dLLM served with threshold-based parallel decoding (making the method inapplicable), or if forced-commitment behavior on the reader's tasks differs from LLaDA/Dream benchmarks. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: AgentBouncer: Defending Software Engineering Agents via Dynamic System-Call Mediation
item.description: AgentBouncer replaces prompt- and trajectory-level defenses, which inspect only the initial prompt and tool-call sequence, with an LLM arbiter that mediates the actual system calls an agent triggers, gated by preseeded policy rules and hierarchy-aware caching. It costs about 47 seconds and USD 0.0036 per benign task, plus the engineering effort of integrating a syscall-interception layer into the agent's tool execution path. It can fail against attacks outside its evaluated four vectors, through arbiter misjudgment of necessity or safety on novel tasks, and if cache hits silently propagate an incorrect prior allow/deny decision. 0 independent implementations, 1 star. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Oops!... I Parsed It Again: Tool-Call Smuggling Against LLM Agents
item.description: The defense replaces the common pattern where provider, gateway, guard, and executor each independently parse the same raw tool-call bytes with a single parse (including JSON embedded in string arguments), projection onto the approved schema, and a canonical call sealed with its call ID that the executor uses directly. Cost is modest implementation complexity in the agent pipeline and the loss of any implicit flexibility from tolerating parser-ambiguous input; latency and memory overhead are negligible. It fails if any component bypasses the canonical representation, if schemas are too permissive (e.g., extra fields a malicious server adds that the model fills with user data), or if non-JSON channels are added later without the same treatment. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Uncovering the Tells: Efficient Black-Box Audits for LLM Data Contamination
item.description: The method replaces full-sequence sampling and uniform-position sampling heuristics for black-box training-data contamination audits with a generation-based framework that targets the few highly informative tokens carrying the membership signal. It costs implementation complexity for the token-targeting policy and still incurs per-query API inference expense, though roughly 3x less than uniform sampling. It can fail when the sparsity assumption does not hold for a given model or dataset, and results on closed frontier models remain exploratory, so contamination findings may be inconclusive or non-actionable. 0 independent implementations, 6 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: MTL-MHOL: Predicting Online Conversions under Delayed Feedback and Data Sparsity
item.description: MTL-MHOL replaces single-task CVR models that handle delayed conversions or data sparsity separately (e.g., plain ESMM or importance-weighting baselines) with a unified time-bucketing plus multi-task auxiliary-learning framework that wraps an existing backbone such as MLP or DeepFM. It costs additional pipeline complexity: maintaining time buckets, training an auxiliary task, and online-learning updates, though compute per se is modest and fits a single small GPU or even CPU-class training. It can fail if conversion-delay distributions drift, if the auxiliary task is poorly correlated with the conversion target, or if the proprietary-dataset gains do not transfer to the reader's traffic, since evidence is limited to one private dataset and Criteo. 0 independent implementations, 33 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Transport-Safe Evaluation of LLM Agents: Trajectory-Dependent Judge Error and Anytime-Valid Auditing
item.description: This replaces one-time scalar judge calibration applied uniformly across agents with per-agent error correction via augmented inverse-probability weighting over randomly audited trajectories, plus anytime-valid e-process monitoring. It costs an ongoing human audit budget (hundreds to thousands of sampled trajectory labels), added estimation complexity, and yields only bounds or rank sets when calibration support is insufficient. It can fail when the audit sampling design lacks support over the target trajectory distribution, when the judge dependence exceeds justified sensitivity bounds, or when the comparison target drifts during adaptive auditing. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Intent-Conditioned Argument Mediation for Tool-Using LLM Agents: Blocking Trusted-but-Unauthorized Arguments
item.description: IntentFlow replaces argument-level provenance-only mediation (or CaMeL-style capability checks) with a mediation layer that validates each authority-bearing tool argument against an explicit intent contract plus a provenance policy, without modifying the planner. It costs the engineering of per-tool intent contracts and provenance policies, an added check in the tool-call path, and dependency on intent/injection oracles whose real-world equivalents must be built and maintained. It can fail by residual attacks on content or payload fields (all 24 remaining successes were of this type), by over-blocking hard benign tasks (4 of 50), and wherever intent cannot be specified precisely enough to distinguish authorized from trusted-but-unrequested arguments. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: GameDojo: Benchmarking Real-Time Interactive Agents in Video Games
item.description: GameDojo replaces ad hoc or non-interactive agent evaluations with a controlled benchmark of 120 boss encounters across 20 games, plus 600 hours of gameplay trajectories for training and evaluation. Adoption costs include engineering effort to reconstruct and run the environments, compute for real-time rollouts, and, if used for training, fine-tuning a 4B model on the trajectory data. It can fail as a proxy: gains on game bosses may not transfer to business tasks, and models can overfit the benchmark without improving general interactive competence. 0 independent implementations, 138 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Doc-to-LoRA Analysis: Query Conditioning, Wrong Facts, and Distractor Interference
item.description: Doc-to-LoRA replaces repeated in-context processing of memory documents by compiling them into low-rank adapters that are merged into the model, eliminating per-query document tokens. It costs answer accuracy: D2L loses to in-context learning on Gemma-2-2B and Qwen3-4B, interference grows with bank size, and on PersonaMem-v2 it only approaches consolidated text memory when retrieved episodes remain as text, yielding modest token savings and hardware-dependent throughput gains. After adoption, multi-document banks can fail through cross-document interference and unreliable question-answer attribution, where answers to one question are contaminated by other questions or passages, and errors accumulate across layers in ways trained readers do not resolve. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: The KL Divergence Is Never Negative, Except in PyTorch
item.description: The method replaces conventional closed-form KL formulas and PyTorch F.kl_div with stable decompositions, compensated arithmetic, and analytic gradients that avoid catastrophic cancellation when comparing nearby distributions. Cost is limited to integrating the released stablekl library and re-validating existing KL-dependent code; there is no additional memory, latency, or infrastructure requirement. What can fail is incomplete coverage if the reader uses KL variants outside the 18 repaired families, and existing models trained under the biased gradients may shift behavior once losses are corrected, requiring re-tuning of hyperparameters that were implicitly calibrated to the old errors. 1 independent implementation, 14 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: How Do Deep Networks Encode and Selectively Use Information? Shared Encoding and Conditional Signed Readout in Vision and Language Models
item.description: The method replaces heuristic or magnitude-based channel-importance scoring with a criterion combining conditional channel variance and fixed downstream readout weights, and replaces generic activation patching with signed channel/pathway decomposition for interpreting edits. It costs substantial per-model analysis effort: perturbation experiments, disjoint block probing, and unit-group selection, with no turnkey implementation or validated pipeline for arbitrary production models. It can fail because the findings are demonstrated on specific convolutional classifiers, one vision transformer, and Qwen2.5 with particular prompt setups; antagonistic-unit structure and prompt-presentation reversals may not transfer, and misidentified signed groups could degrade rather than preserve pruned-model behavior. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Useful but Unwieldy: How Software Engineers Perceive the Design of Chain-of-Thought Explanations in Coding Agents
item.description: This qualitative study replaces the default practice of exposing raw, verbose chain-of-thought messages as the sole transparency mechanism in coding agents. It costs only interface and prompt design effort, since it is a UX/design recommendation rather than a computational technique. It can fail because engineers selectively read or abandon CoT displays when they are overly verbose, mismatched to the user's expertise, or perceived as detached self-talk, so adoption requires tailored summarization and trust calibration rather than full CoT exposure. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Carried-Over and Agent-Native Threats in the Supply Chain of LLM Agent Skills
item.description: The work replaces reliance on dependency CVE alerts as the primary skill-vetting signal with static analysis and sandbox reachability testing of first-party skill code, showing dependency CVEs are reachable in only 3.0% of affected skills while 21 of 22 sampled first-party flaws were exploitable end to end. The cost is engineering effort to run static screening and sandboxed execution tests on skills before deployment, plus runtime changes so skill arguments never pass through a shell. What can fail: the study covers one registry (ClawHub) and sampled reachability tests, so results may not transfer to other registries, and static detectors plus manual review can still miss novel vulnerability classes. 1 independent implementation, 5 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Self-Evolving Evaluation Environments for Computer-Use Agents
item.description: CUA-SEE replaces static, fixed-difficulty computer-use agent benchmarks with a closed-loop environment that co-evolves tasks, diagnostic probes, and executable verifiers from agent rollout evidence. The cost is substantial engineering and compute: running repeated agent rollouts, generating state-grounded checkpoints, and adversarially validating verifiers requires application environments and orchestration well beyond a single 24 GB GPU. What can fail is verifier quality itself — automatically generated checkpoints may be mis-specified or gameable, so the benchmark can mismeasure capability and produce misleading difficulty calibration. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: MedUIGym: Evaluating and Training GUI Agents for Clinical Workflows
item.description: MedUIGym replaces ad hoc, text-only evaluation of clinical GUI agents with a unified interactive environment of 15,739 tasks spanning six clinical task families, dual GUI/native-tool interfaces, and verified final answers and actions. The cost to the reader is substantial: meaningful use requires running or hosting EHR sandbox infrastructure, collecting parallel GUI trajectories, and, for the training results, fine-tuning and RL over vision-language models at a scale that exceeds a single 24 GB GPU without external APIs. What can fail is transfer: the headline finding is that twelve current vision-language models struggle on these workflows and that increased reasoning effort yields no consistent gains, so even successful in-domain training may not translate into reliable production behavior on real, non-sandbox EHR systems with different layouts and latency characteristics. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: RoboUniverse-10K: Toward the Scaling Era of Agentic Robotics via Real-to-Sim Environments
item.description: RoboUniverse-10K replaces small, manually built robotics benchmarks with 10,807 automatically generated Real2Sim verifiable environments, plus a 35B-A3B model fine-tuned on 17K GPT-6 Astra trajectories, supplanting in-distribution evaluation and imitation from small demos. The cost is substantial: an automated video-to-simulation pipeline, privileged-state harness infrastructure, full-parameter SFT of a 35B-A3B MoE model, and access to a frontier teacher model for trajectory generation. Sim-to-real transfer can fail since environments derive from real videos with imperfect physics reconstruction, and the remaining 78.8% failure rate is concentrated in grasping, deformable objects, and post-contact control, so the fine-tuned model is not deployment-ready for physical robots. 1 independent implementation, 253 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: AI-Assisted Auto-formalization for Trustworthy Scientific Computing: Case Studies and Lessons Learned
item.description: The technique replaces fully manual formalization of scientific computing procedures in proof assistants with AI-agent-assisted auto-formalization guided by layered expert feedback. It costs expert review effort at every abstraction layer of the software stack, plus API usage for coding or mathematics agents, and adds workflow complexity without any reported quantitative speedup. It can fail through agent errors that vary by stack layer, particularly where the source describes a computational procedure rather than a declarative theorem, requiring expert intervention to restore mathematical soundness. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: ChiProgramBench: Can LLM Agents Rebuild Efficient Circuits from Pin-Level Experiments?
item.description: The benchmark replaces ad hoc or proxy evaluations of LLM agents' system-understanding ability with a reproducible pin-level circuit reconstruction testbed of 18 tasks with hidden stateful references. Adopting it costs simulation infrastructure, agent API spend across many trials, and gate-level netlist verification expertise, none of which serves typical ML production work. Its results show current agents rarely succeed (roughly 12-15% full pass rates) and almost never improve efficiency, so any workflow assuming agents can autonomously reverse-engineer or optimize hardware would fail. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: NoveltyGate: Novelty, Not Error, Decides Which VLA Prefix Tokens to Compute Exactly
item.description: NoveltyGate replaces full-precision MLP computation for all VLA prefix tokens with per-layer routing that sends most tokens through a low-rank MLP and computes exactly only those whose inputs fall outside the calibration subspace, with static shapes enabling a single CUDA graph. It costs a calibration step to estimate the seen subspace, added routing complexity, and reliance on the finding that novelty, not approximation error, predicts which tokens the policy depends on. It can fail if the calibration distribution does not match deployment inputs, if the error-reliance gap does not hold for a different VLA model or camera configuration, or if the 1.61x prefix speedup translates to a smaller end-to-end gain once non-prefix compute dominates. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: LiveLoRA: Exact KV Cache Migration Across LoRA Updates for LLM Agents
item.description: LiveLoRA replaces full-history re-prefill when updating a LoRA adapter for active sessions by migrating the final-block KV cache exactly, exploiting frozen lower decoder blocks and fixed K/V down-projections so that adapter, cache, and logits are committed together. It costs approximately 4.8% decoding overhead, imposes structural constraints on the model (frozen lower blocks and fixed K/V adapter projections across versions), and adds runtime complexity for candidate K/V reconstruction and reevaluation of the latest token. It can fail if the model or adapter setup violates these assumptions, if exact-arithmetic equivalence is broken by numerical or implementation divergence, or if the validated regime (a 3B model, 32 sessions, 8K-token histories) does not match the reader's production scale or model family. 1 independent implementation, 126 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Look Back, Draft Ahead: Corrective Prefix Attention for Parallel Speculative Decoding
item.description: CPA replaces existing parallel speculative drafters (DSpark, DFlash) by letting block candidates attend to earlier in-block choices via precomputed pairwise interaction tables, avoiding repeated neural evaluations during the sequential selection walk. Its cost is an additional training phase: the shared backbone must be fine-tuned with an auxiliary autoregressive loss on clean prefixes, plus implementation complexity for the shortlist tables, though inference adds no extra forward pass. Failure modes include gains that do not transfer beyond the reported math, code, and dialogue workloads, results measured only on Ascend NPUs with Qwen3-4B/8B, the authors' own finding that higher acceptance does not guarantee faster decoding, and possible unavailability of portable open-source implementations. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: ACAP: Asynchronous Coding Agents for Efficient Robot Control
item.description: ACAP replaces a single monolithic coding agent controlling an entire robot with a team of persistent per-component agents coordinated by a hyper-agent that assigns tasks and arbitrates physical dependencies. It costs substantially more LLM inference per rollout, persistent agent state, and coordination logic, with added system complexity over a direct policy. It can fail through hyper-agent misallocation or unresolved physical dependencies between control groups, and the reported gains rest on only 72 to 90 rollouts, so reliability at scale is unverified. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: A Mixed-Methods Study of Personal Software Creation
item.description: The study does not replace an engineering method; it surveys 6,168 web and Reddit posts and observes eight users building personal software with AI coding agents, characterizing the workflow as functionality emerging reactively during building and creator effort shifting from writing code to checking it. Adoption cost is not applicable, though the workflow it describes implies verification effort becomes the dominant human cost. The principal failure mode it implies is defective or mis-specified software when users cannot effectively check agent-generated code. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Language Models Steer on Injected Uncertainty Tokens, but Fail to Self-Monitor In Situ
item.description: This replaces self-verbalized stepwise confidence as the trigger for backtracking in agentic reasoning, which the paper shows fails as a monitoring signal, with external detection of error steps followed by injection of an explicit low-confidence token or rethinking instruction. The cost is an additional error-detection component (a verifier, separate model pass, or heuristic) plus extra generation for revised continuations, adding latency and API spend, and the self-monitoring prompting itself provides no usable signal. Injected doubt can cause the model to discard already-correct reasoning, reducing solve rates by up to 22.8 points, so the approach fails when the external detector produces false alarms on sound steps. 1 independent implementation, 130 stars. Research area: failure recovery. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Pruning Autonomous Driving VLAs: What to Preserve for Reasoning and Action
item.description: MoOP replaces uniform or single-objective structured pruning of reasoning VLA models with rank-fused importance from both reasoning and trajectory objectives for the VLM, plus stepwise-aggregated selection of a fixed subset of action-expert MLP channels. It requires access to and pruning of the Alpamayo-1.5-10B base model and incurs a quality cost: about 6% LingoQA loss at 24% parameter reduction, with reasoning collapse risk deferred but not eliminated at 30% reduction. The approach can fail if applied to models or tasks where the two objectives' importance rankings do not transfer, and closed-loop driving metrics still degrade relative to the dense model despite preserved open-loop accuracy. 2 independent implementations, 69 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Epistemic Guard: Out-of-Process MCP Receipt Proxying, Post-Turn Prose Supervision, and Provenance-Gated Memory for Tool-Using Autonomous Agents
item.description: The method replaces LLM-judge guardrails and pre-execution MCP firewalls with an out-of-process stdio receipt proxy that Ed25519-signs and Merkle-logs tool calls, verifies post-turn prose against receipts on CPU via INT8 encoders, and gates durable-memory writes by provenance. It costs no GPU VRAM (279.48 MB of CPU models, 82.67 MB on the supervision path), adds roughly 9-18 ms median CPU latency per turn plus a 921.8 ms cold start, and introduces proxy-side operational complexity including key isolation and SQLite gating. After adoption, the main failure risk is the 38.24% false positive rate on live traffic, which can block legitimate actions and degrade agent usability, and the 76.67% live accuracy indicates residual missed or misjudged hazards outside frozen benchmarks. 1 independent implementation, 5 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Omo: Giving Continuing AI-Agent Work a Place to Return To
item.description: Omo replaces flat session lists with persistent spatial workspaces (a Minecraft mod and an IDE integration) that keep coding-agent sessions running on the host and let a returning user see what was asked, what changed, and what to do next. It costs integration effort and host resources for continuously running sessions, plus the complexity of adopting an open-source mod or a custom IDE surface rather than an existing agent console; no performance or usability results are reported, only a study design. It can fail if spatial organization adds overhead without improving resumption accuracy, if users do not adopt the custom environments, or if unattended host-resident sessions drift or conflict with the local repository state. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Markdown Is Not a Firewall: four coding agents, one rules file, four boundaries
item.description: Replaces trust in repository rules files (e.g., AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md) as a security or compliance control with deterministic gates in front of sensitive endpoints, plus hidden-test-based evaluation. Cost is low in compute but requires building gate infrastructure around tool calls and accepting that a rules file may reduce agent task performance (Codex CLI: 99.0 to 67.7 percent). Failure modes: the study could not test the file's effect at HTTP boundaries due to a run-script error, results cover four agents and small repositories, and planted-package/instruction risks remain if no gate exists (7 of 45 ungated runs crossed). 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: CoEvoBench: Can LLMs Drive Recursive Co-Evolution of Agentic Systems?
item.description: CoEvoBench replaces separate, single-component agent evaluations with a joint benchmark in which an LLM researcher iteratively decides whether to modify the model or the harness under a 24-hour compute budget. Running it costs substantial frontier-model API usage plus training compute within that budget, which is beyond a single 24 GB GPU setup. Its central finding is a failure mode: LLM researchers produce a strong first improvement but cannot convert feedback from the improved system into further gains, so co-evolution pipelines built on this premise will plateau quickly. 1 independent implementation, 130 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Double counting in LLM evidence fusion: exact posteriors separate rule compliance from posterior gain
